item.title: Wednesday Seacoast Roundup: Portsmouth field hockey season ends in DI prelim, more results
item.description: LONDONDERRY — The ninth-seeded Portsmouth High School field hockey team saw its season come to an end, falling to No. 9 Londonderry, 2-0, in a Division I preliminary-round game on Wednesday, Oct. 21. "I am extremely impressed with how hard our team played today," Portsmouth head coach Allison St. Jean said. "They continued the drive until the very end." Portsmouth ended its season with a record of 8-8-1. "I am very proud of the effort, determination and growth I continue to see in the Portsmouth field hockey players," St. Jean said. "This is our third season playing in Division I, and we continue to improve with each season. This is truly a season that each and every one of our players should be proud of." Londonderry broke through first when Emma Karielis scored with 6:31 remaining in the first quarter, then added an insurance goal in the fourth quarter when Morgan Ayotte scored with 13:30 left. Portsmouth sophomore goalkeeper Charlotte Daboul had 10 saves. GIRLS SOCCER Portsmouth Christian Academy 6 Epping 1 DOVER - Jaela Stockbower scored three goals, and Tilly Arico had two goals and one assist for PCA (14-1) in its Division IV contest. Brie Mullins also scored a goal for the Eagles, and Svea Howe had two assists. BOYS SOCCER Newmarket 2 Franklin 0 FRANKLIN - Sawyer Rabb and Aiden Ekanem scored for Newmarket (14-0-2) in its Division IV win. -Coaches are asked to e-mail game summaries to sports@seacoastonline.com. item.title: Former Celtic manager reveals where Hoops would finish in Premier League
item.description: Former Celtic manager reveals where Hoops would finish in Premier League Former Celtic manager Gordon Strachan believes the Hoops and Rangers would struggle to compete in the English Premier League. The 69-year-old, who guided Celtic to three consecutive Scottish Premiership titles during his four-year spell at Parkhead, has offered a pessimistic assessment of how Scotland’s two biggest clubs would fare south of the border. Despite Celtic’s history of competing against some of Europe’s biggest clubs, Strachan believes the financial gulf between Scottish and English football would make life particularly difficult. item.title: Ohtani surgery 'not on the table': Dodgers chief
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers say Shohei Ohtani will not need surgery during the offseason after the Japanese superstar's injury-hit 2026 campaign (Sean M. Haffey) The Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday ruled out off-season surgery for Shohei Ohtani following the Japanese superstar's injury-hit end to the season. An ailing Ohtani's poor form was blamed as one of the key factors for the Dodgers' failed playoff campaign, which ended in a 4-0 series sweep to the Milwaukee Brewers last week. Ohtani, 32, had struggled with knee and biceps problems since July, and the Dodgers have faced scrutiny over their management of the four-time Most Valuable Player's injuries leading into the playoffs. But while some commentators have questioned whether Ohtani's grueling pitching and hitting workload was behind his dip in form, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday Ohtani would continue to pitch next season. Friedman told reporters that surgery for Ohtani was "not on the table" as he described the star's injuries as a game of "whack-a-mole. "He had a lot of different stuff going on," Friedman said of Ohtani. His knee was bothering him off and on. "It was a little bit of an unfortunate game of whack-a-mole. The knee would get to a good spot and then the bicep was bothering him. It was a number of different things – some that would calm down for a period, some that would get re-irritated." Ohtani, whose elite pitching and hitting talents have seen him acclaimed by some as the greatest player in baseball history, was believed to have been targeting a Cy Young pitching award in 2026 before his injuries left him unable to pitch. Friedman said while the Dodgers wanted Ohtani to pitch next season, the team would develop a strategy that allowed their star player to reach the postseason in peak form. "I'm not only expecting him to pitch, I'm excited about him pitching," Friedman said. "So now it's a question of how do we manage a long season and have him at his best going into October. That's the challenge and we've got to figure it out together." In statistical terms, Ohtani's figures in 2026 marked his worst since signing for the Dodgers in 2023. After lashing 54 and 55 home runs in his first two regular season campaigns with the Dodgers in 2024 and 2025, Ohtani cracked only 30 homers this year. His batting average dipped to .275, down from 2024 (.310) and 2025 (.282). rcw/bb

item.title: Cursed, Fight, Score: Tkachuk Has Eventful Opening Period Back in Ottawa
item.description: Brady Tkachuk went through a whole range of emotions in the first period of his return to Ottawa to face his former Senators teammates on Wednesday night with the Florida Panthers. Tkachuk, who spent eight seasons with the Senators, was booed during warmups and throughout the opening period. Although there were some audible cheers during his video tribute — ‘Thank You, Brady Tkachuk!’ the public address announcer said at the end — there were mostly jeers. Ottawa fans came prepared with a variety of chants aimed at their former captain who forced a summertime divorce and moved to the tropics . One was as simple as it was profane: ‘F-You Brady!’ Not long after Tkachuk’s tribute video aired but he got some payback by scoring on Florida’s first shot of the night on a power-play chance at the 10-minute mark. Brady scored, poetically enough, off a pass from brother Matthew . Brady hit 'em with the 🤷‍♂️ ! pic.twitter.com/sQQw74OTg3 — Jameson Olive (@JamesonCoop) October 22, 2026 Later in the period, Brady got involved in a scrum behind the goal in which he and now-former teammate Shane Pinto traded words — and fists. Brady Tkachuk spent 2 minutes in the penalty box for that one. The Panthers and Senators went into the first break tied at 1. item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Christian Darrisaw #71 of the Minnesota Vikings lines up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Vikings fans and fans across the country. It’s time for this week’s installment of our SB Nation Reacts survey about our Minnesota Vikings, ladies and gentlemen. The polls have been up over in the Feed for a little bit already, but we’re putting them up here on the main page now for a bit more visibility for folks who might not check over there all that regularly. We’ve got two questions for you this week. The first one, as always, is how confident you are that our favorite team is moving in the right direction. Just like they were going into their bye week, our Minnesota Vikings are one of just three teams in the NFL who are without a loss and one of just two teams who are sitting at 5-0 at this point in the season. The offense still may not be clicking on all cylinders, but the defense and special teams certainly have been, so we want to know how good you’re feeling now that we’re moving into the post-bye portion of the schedule. Speaking of feeling good, the Vikings are going to have some important names coming back from injury starting this Sunday when they face off against the Indianapolis Colts. Namely wide receiver Jordan Addison, offensive tackle Christian Darrisaw, tight end T.J. Hockenson, and running back Jordan Mason. All of them missed the game against New Orleans in Week 5. . .well, technically Hockenson didn’t miss the game, but his afternoon was done after two snaps because of a concussion, so for all intents and purposes, he missed the game. As Warren told you earlier this afternoon , all four of those guys were full participants in Wednesday’s first practice of the week, so it would appear they’re all on track to return to the field on Sunday. So, which of those guys is the most important for the purple to get back into the huddle? As always, we invite you to make your voice heard on these topics by voting in our polls, whether it’s here or in the Feed, and sounding off in the comments section. Have at it, everybody! We’ll have the results of these polls for you sometime before kickoff on Sunday afternoon. Whose return will be most important? Are you confident in the Vikings? Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. (CBS) at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California. The Big Ten released its first availability report Wednesday night, and it will be updated two more times before the final report two hours before the game begins. The unspecified Milivojevic injury situation could be a significant issue if he cannot play. Backup quarterback Cam Fancher remains out, and first-year freshman Kayd Coffman served as the No. 2 quarterback the past two weeks in losses to Illinois and Northwestern. Coffman got his first snaps as a college player late in MSU’s loss at Wisconsin after Fancher got hurt and left the game with an apparent knee injury. item.title: São Paulo suffer defeat and bow out of Women's Copa do Brasil
item.description: São Paulo suffer defeat and bow out of Women's Copa do Brasil On Wednesday (21), São Paulo lost 1–0 to Bahia at Estádio Brinco de Ouro da Princesa in Campinas, São Paulo, in the second leg of the Women's Copa do Brasil quarterfinals. The first half began evenly, with both teams attacking at a high tempo from the outset. In the 19th minute, São Paulo had a chance to take the lead through Kesia Sena, who received the ball in her own half and surged forward. The number 18 found herself one-on-one with goalkeeper Yanne but shot wide. In the 27th minute, Mylena received the ball inside the box, rounded the opposing goalkeeper and fired a low shot, only for a defender to clear it. The first half ended goalless. Just six minutes into the second half, Cássia scored for Bahia. São Paulo tried to turn things around throughout the rest of the match, but it ended 1–0 to Bahia. São Paulo had lost the first leg 2–1. With a 3–1 aggregate defeat, São Paulo bowed out of the Copa do Brasil. Tricolor's next match will be away to Santos on November 17 at 7 p.m. in the Women's São Paulo State Championship. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Adam Amin pays emotional tribute to Stacey King at Bulls opener
item.description: Credit: CHSN As they tipped off their season on Wednesday night, the Chicago Bulls are missing longtime franchise legend Stacey King. King passed away in June at the age of 59 after two decades as a broadcaster and winning three championships as a player with the franchise. He was beloved for his colorful analysis and enthusiasm as an announcer and accomplishments as a player, where his #33 was retired at Oklahoma in addition to his success with the Bulls. It was always going to be an emotional beginning to the season and the tribute from the Bulls broadcast was powerful with play-by-play announcer Adam Amin voicing a video tribute to Stacey King on the Chicago Sports Network with highlights of their time together before their season opener in Toronto against the Raptors. “I know exactly who he was, I know what his gift could do, and I know that we were all just a little happier, a little better off, for getting to hear the song…for as long as we did.” @adamamin gives a touching tribute to his late partner, Stacey King https://t.co/VPRP58XjOA — Bulls on CHSN (@CHSN_Bulls) October 21, 2026 Poetically, the Bulls held King’s seat vacant for the first quarter of the Raptors game with Amin calling the game solo. A crown and one of King’s playing cards was present on the vacant seat next to the announcer as he welcomed fans to the broadcast. https://t.co/V7SeJoTTK8 — Bulls on CHSN (@CHSN_Bulls) October 21, 2026 “We love you very much, Stacey. And we appreciate everything you did for us, everything you did with us. And for this opening quarter of this opening game of this season, we’ll leave this chair next to our broadcast position empty. And we’ll give it a little bit of an acknowledgement and a hat tip, and perhaps a little bit of a jarring realization that he’s not with us anymore. And that’s ok, and it will be ok eventually,” Amin said. The Bulls plan to use a rotation of analysts throughout the season to fulfill analyst duties. After the vacant first quarter, Robbie Hummel served as the game analyst alongside Amin for the opening contest. Analysts may be present throughout the season, but this was a powerful reminder that nobody could truly fill Stacey King’s seat this year. item.description: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis hasn't met Steve Kerr © X/@warriors The aging Golden State Warriors enter this season hoping to at least be in the mix for playoff contention. However, they were hit with troubling news on Wednesday as reports emerged that veteran big man Kristaps Porzingis is seriously contemplating retirement due to health issues. NBA insider Shams Charania reported on Wednesday that the Warriors have started shopping Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autonomic condition known as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome). Porzingis signed with the Warriors on a two-year, $40 million deal but has been away from team activities due to these recurring medical issues. He has not practiced with the team in training camp nor appeared in any preseason games. It only makes sense that the Warriors will look to explore trade options, as they want to remain competitive in the dwindling window of the Steph Curry era. While many have speculated on who Golden State could target, Milwaukee-based podcaster Ti Windisch suggested Bucks center Myles Turner as a viable candidate to keep an eye on. “Keep an eye on Myles Turner to Golden State as an option here. Warriors have nearly all of their picks and clearly desired a stretch 5 to pair with Curry/Draymond,” Windisch wrote on X. Adding another layer is that the Giants are traveling to Houston, where McCarthy won the National Championship with Jim Harbaugh’s Michigan Wolverines in 2024, a fact that isn’t lost on McCarthy. “It is really special, it’s awesome,” he said. “But each game, each rep is an independent event. And going in there and just focusing on that first play and executing those six seconds within that play, that’s really the main focus. But it’s going to be really cool to be in Houston and I think we’re staying in the same hotel that we stayed in when we were there in 2024.” McCarthy doesn’t have time to get caught up in sentimentality, however. It’s going to be awesome to just ask him really anything and pick his brain about anything.” Speaking of the offense, McCarthy adds an element of athleticism to the quarterback position that was lost with Dart against the Los Angeles Rams. He also adds a speed contrast to the Giants’ more power-oriented backfield. And at the end of the day, I approach it the same way. How can I attack that next rep, how can I win this day and go from there.”

item.title: Aaron Glenn’s praise of Frank Reich invites scrutiny
item.description: FOXBOROUGH, MA - OCTOBER 18: Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets during a game between the New England Patriots and the New York Jets on October 18, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots, offensive coordinator Frank Reich has been a target of fan and media criticism for his playcalling. Head coach Aaron Glenn said positive things about Reich’s performance to the media on Wednesday. Asked if the offensive struggles might prompt him to get more involved in helping Frank Reich, Aaron Glenn said he's always collaborating with his coordinators on ways to improve. He also said we should "acknowledge" some of the positives on offense. He mentioned their explosive… — Rich Cimini (@RichCimini) October 21, 2026 Asked if the offensive struggles might prompt him to get more involved in helping Frank Reich, Aaron Glenn said he’s always collaborating with his coordinators on ways to improve. He also said we should “acknowledge” some of the positives on offense. He mentioned their explosive plays on play-action (six pass plays of 20+ yards, T-9th) and an improved run game (12th in rushing over last two weeks). #Jets Glenn noting explosive plays off play action in combination with the run game is interesting to me. Many offensive coordinators effectively build their deep passing game off their run game and play action. And according to the advanced stats at Pro Football Reference , the Jets have the fourth best average per passing attempt off play action in the league through the season’s first six weeks. However, only 22% of Jets passes come off play action per PFR, which is 21st highest in the league. What stands out to me is how often the Jets offense stalls on drives after a series of consecutive runs. This began in Week 1 when the Jets were forced to settle for a field goal after a 19 play drive. Against New England, the Jets had three first half drives stall out after a series four consecutive rushes. There has been a pattern of running effectively and then eventually getting stopped instead of building to deep shots off play action. I understand the argument that the Jets’ efficiency on play action might be aided by how infrequently they use it. It might catch opponents by surprise to a degree. Still, it’s notable to hear Glenn cite play action performance to defend his play caller, when there is some evidence that Reich isn’t leaning into it enough.

"It feels amazing, especially because I've played Jolie so many times. I played her three times last season, and I lost all three times," Amurao said. "Especially at sectionals last year, I lost really badly. I felt better going into this year since we had a close match earlier in the season, and I won that match." "She believed," said Scotia-Glenville head coach Geoff Olson. "I've never had a player, girl or boy, prepare and want it as much as her." Amurao trailed Shen sophomore Chichak early on in both sets of the championship match, but was able to find her way back. item.title: Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt Injury Report: Sam Greene likely out; CJ Baxter set to play
item.description: The Kentucky Wildcats and Vanderbilt Commodores have released their first injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup Saturday night at Kroger Field. The big news is that standout linebacker Sam Greene is doubtful to play. Greene has played in every game this season after recovering from an ACL tear suffered toward the end of last season. Hopefully, this is not a significant issue and he’ll be able to return coming out of the Wildcats’ Week 9 bye. Running back CJ Baxter, who dressed for the Oklahoma game but was held out, is listed as probable, so he should play. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who left Saturday’s win in Norman late due to an injury, is listed as questionable, so there’s a 50-50 shot he plays for the time being. Linebacker Tavion Wallace, who’s missed the last three games, tweeted on Wednesday that he’d returned to practice, so that could be a boost to a position that’s been thin. Wallace is officially listed as probable. Fellow linebacker Antawn Smith, who was injured at South Carolina and missed the last two games, has been ruled out for this week. Cornerback Grant Grayton remains out. Cornerback Jaden Smith, who was also injured at South Carolina and hasn’t played since, has been ruled out. Defensive tackle Kalen Edwards is probable. Defensive end Tyler Thomas is questionable. Finally, long-snapper Cole Marszalek is listed as doubtful to play. For Vanderbilt, starting cornerback Cayden Daniels is probable. Backup defensive end Brian Allen Jr. is listed as out. Backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, who opened the season as the starter before being benched, injured his collarbone in Week 6 vs. Ole Miss and remains listed as out. Backup defensive end Haydon Brey is probable. Backup linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful to play. Backup safeties Dontae Carter and Devin Chandler are listed as questionable. Backup guard Mitchell Smith is probable. Finally, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant, linebacker Jamison Curtis, offensive lineman Gunner Givens, defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, and wide receiver Kahden Smith are out this week. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
